brackets.section: Form MO-1040ES Tax Rate Chart, page 2
brackets.note: One schedule for every filing status, so head of household uses it too. Tax Foundation and PolicyEngine show the same thresholds and the 4.7% top rate. The chart prints "$263 plus 4.7% of excess over $9,436"; these brackets give $262.86, which the chart rounds to whole dollars.

earnedIncomeCredit.section: RSMo 143.177.3(1); department FAQ, "20% for tax year 2024 and forward"
earnedIncomeCredit.note: 20% of the federal credit, and "the difference shall not be refunded to the taxpayer and shall not be carried forward". The statute bases it on section 32 as of January 1, 2021, but the 2025 form takes 20% of the credit on the federal return and adds an investment income limit ($4,400 for 2025), which is not checked.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: Missouri working family tax credit

standardDeduction.note: Missouri uses the federal standard deduction amounts. These are the 2026 figures printed on the form. Tax Foundation agrees for single and joint.

personalExemption.note: Missouri has no personal or dependent exemption (Tax Foundation shows n.a.). The only amount is a $1,400 additional exemption for head of household and qualifying widow(er) filers, read from the form.

federalTaxDeduction.note: Share of federal income tax (after credits, ignoring the refundable child credit) that is deductible, by Missouri AGI: 35% up to $25,000, 25% up to $50,000, 15% up to $100,000, 5% up to $125,000, nothing above. From PolicyEngine, which cites the MO-1040 instructions and RSMo 143.171. The statute also caps the deduction ($5,000, or $10,000 on a combined return; PolicyEngine lists $10,000 for every status but separate). No cap is entered because at these shares a wage earner cannot reach either figure. Checked against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 with oracle/compare.py on 2026-11-12.

rules.note: Kansas City's 1% earnings tax is from Tax Foundation's table. The federal tax deduction tiers were checked against RSMo 143.171: at exactly $100,000 the 15% tier applies, where PolicyEngine gives 5%. Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions, apart from the case that lands on the $100,000 boundary. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions. No employee payroll contribution: the US Department of Labor's comparison lists worker unemployment contributions only in Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and disability insurance only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, and no paid leave or similar program with an employee contribution was found for this state on 2026-11-12.
notes: Kansas City and St. Louis levy city earnings taxes on wages. Not included.
Missouri lets filers deduct part of their federal income tax: 35% at Missouri AGI up to $25,000, falling in steps to nothing above $125,000. This is included.

Not modeled: on a combined return each spouse computes tax separately on their share of the income (Form MO-1040ES, lines 9 and 10), so a two-earner couple gets the lower brackets twice. The effect is under $200.
